summary: Walter Elliot worked in Indology, linguistics, and history and archaeology. He studied at East India Company College (~1818–1820) and the College of Fort St George (~1821–1823), later serving as Private Secretary to Lord Elphinstone in the Madras Government (1837–1842).

Walter Eugene Clark was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his A.B. and doctorate at Harvard (~1899–1906) and studied under Richard Pischel (~1906–1907). He taught at the University of Chicago (1923–1927) and Harvard (1927–1950).

Walter Evans-Wentz was a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Stanford University (~1903–1907), Jesus College, Oxford (1907–1911), and as a disciple under Kazi Dawa Samdup (~1919–1922).

Walter Liebenthal worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. After studies at Berlin, Marburg, Heidelberg, Halle, and Breslau (Dr. phil ~1933), he held posts at Peking University, Visva-Bharati University, Hebrew University, Sorbonne, and University of Tübingen (1965–1982).

Walter M. Spink was an Indologist and scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Amherst College (~1945–1949) and Harvard (PhD ~1949–1954). He taught at Brandeis (1956–1961) before his long professorship at the University of Michigan (~1961–2019).

Walter Nowick was a Buddhist studies practitioner and teacher who studied at the Juilliard School and under Zuigan Goto (1950–1965). He served on the faculty at Kyoto Women's University and founded Moonspring Hermitage.

Walter Piston studied at Massachusetts College of Art and Design (~1912–1916) and Harvard University (~1920–1924). He subsequently served on the faculty at Harvard University from around 1926 to 1960.

Walter Porzig was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Jena (~1914–1920) and under Wilhelm Streitberg (~1919–1921). He held positions at Leipzig, Bern, Jena, and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1951–1961).
Walter Ruben was a scholar in Indology. He held academic posts at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1931–1935), the University of Chile (~1948–1949), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1950–1965).

Walter Simon specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics. Educated at Humboldt University of Berlin under Otto Franke and August Hermann Francke, he held posts at Berlin, the National Library of China, and the University of London / SOAS (1936–1960).

Walter Slaje is an Indologist who completed his Promotion and Habilitation at the University of Vienna (~1978–1993). He worked at Graz University Library (1984–1995) and served as Director at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1995 to 2020.

Walter William Skeat was a linguist who studied at Highgate School, King's College School, and Christ's College, Cambridge (~1854–1858). He served on the faculty at the University of Cambridge from around 1878 to 1912.

Walther Heissig specialized in Central Asian and religious studies. He studied at Vienna, Berlin, Göttingen, and Bonn. After teaching at Fu Jen Catholic University and Peking University (~1941–1945), he was appointed Chair of the Central Asian seminar at Bonn in 1964.

Walther Schubring was an Indologist who studied at Munich and Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann. After working at the Prussian State Library (1907), he held the Indology chair at the University of Hamburg from 1920 to 1951.

Walther Wüst was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Munich (1920–1923). He later served at Munich as Dean (1935–1945), led a section at Ahnenerbe (1936), and was president of the Deutsche Akademie (1943).

Wannaporn Rienjang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology who completed a PhD at the University of Cambridge. She worked at the British Museum, the Classical Art Research Centre (attested 2019–2022), and Thammasat University (attested 2022–2023).
Warren Cowgill was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Stanford (~1948–1952) and earned his Ph.D. at Yale (~1952–1957). He became a professor of linguistics at Yale University starting in 1956.

Warren Lee Todd works in philosophy and Indology. He earned his PhD at Lancaster University (attested 2012) under Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, having also studied under Irina Kuznetsova, Peter Harvey, and Chogye Trichen Rinpoche.

Warrin Ratanamalai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, studying under Phra Suthithammanuwat, Phra Srisitthimuni, Phra Sudhivorayan, and Phramaha Somjin Sammāpañño.
Watari Yanai was a scholar of Sinology, archaeology, and Central Asian history. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1898–1901) and later held a post there from around 1919 to 1926.
